FINDING_ID: MM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.98
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.87
DESCRIPTION: In [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L430) the Duane convergence parameter is defined as `γ = 1 − β`, but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1789) computes `γ̂ = log(r) / (log |F≤r| − log |F≤1|)`. Under the Duane power law `N(r) ∝ r^β`, that estimator simplifies to `1/β`, not `1−β`. The code therefore flips the model’s interpretation: appendix semantics use `γ > 0` for decreasing finding rate, while the code uses `γ > 1` as the “good” regime.
PROPOSED_FIX: Estimate `β̂ = (log |F≤r| − log |F≤1|) / log(r)` and then set `γ̂ = 1 − β̂`; update the diagnostic thresholds and docstring to match the appendix.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.91
DESCRIPTION: [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L461) defines `Y(t) = N(t) · H̄(t)`, then claims at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L465) that `(dH̄/dt)/H̄ > |dλ/dt|/λ` implies `dY/dt > 0`. That inequality is the condition for `d(λH̄)/dt > 0`, not for `dY/dt > 0`, because `dY/dt = λH̄ + N·dH̄/dt`. The implementation also does not follow the appendix formula: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2265) reduces “ascending abstraction” to a one-step `H̄` comparison and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2271) omits the appendix’s `V̂_remaining < ε` term entirely.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either redefine the guarded quantity as instantaneous value rate `v(t) = λ(t)·H̄(t)` and keep the current relative-growth inequality, or derive the correct condition for `Y(t) = N(t)·H̄(t)`; then align `stop()` to the corrected `stop_valid(t)` formula.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88
DESCRIPTION: The capability fingerprint semantics drift between model and code. [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L610) defines `(D_decay, v̄, A, C)` with `A = total novel verified findings` and `C = A / estimated total real findings`, while [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L281) documents `A` as “Accuracy / alignment” and `C` as “Coverage breadth”, and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5344) actually computes `A` as mean severity and `C` as distinct flaw-class breadth. The symbol `A` is also already used for anchor state in [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L775), so there is both semantic drift and notation collision.
PROPOSED_FIX: Choose one contract and make both artifacts match it. Best option: keep anchor state as `A`, rename fingerprint dimensions to unambiguous symbols, and if §7.9 is authoritative then compute `A` as deduped verified-count and `C` from estimated total real findings rather than severity/class breadth.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L446) defines `H(x)` as an unbounded multiplicative index and gives a verified example `H = 17.89` at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L455), but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L364) defines `abstraction_index` as `H(f) in [0, 1]`. That public code contract cannot represent the appendix’s stated scale, so `Y(t)` and any thresholding built on `H` are not on the same mathematical object.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove the `[0,1]` contract and use raw `H(x)` throughout, or add an explicit normalization map in the appendix and code, such as `H_norm = g(H_raw)`, and state that all downstream code uses the normalized form.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1419) says `aggregated_severity = S_v([f])`, but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1630) computes it as `max(f.severity for f in members)`. That is not the appendix’s Bayesian multi-verifier severity `S_v` from [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L592); it is only a proxy. Because `kappa_set` and the severity veto use this value, convergence behaviour is being driven by a different statistic than the model names.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either compute real class-level `S_v` from verifier outputs, or rename the field to something like `max_member_severity` and update all comments/docs so the code no longer claims equivalence it does not implement.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: The Objective Alignment definition is internally inconsistent. [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L507) defines `O_A = |verified findings in F_conv| / |F_conv|`, but the guard and prose at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L519) and [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L533) say `O_A` should operate on the verifiable subset only. With mixed verifiable and unverifiable findings, the current denominator still penalizes `O_A` for unverifiable items, which reintroduces the exact false-sycophancy failure the guard is supposed to prevent.
PROPOSED_FIX: Redefine `O_A` as `|{f ∈ F_conv : verified(f)}| / |{f ∈ F_conv : verifiable(f)}|`, and keep `O_A = ⊥` when the denominator is less than 2.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33
DESCRIPTION: The worked “Verified” example for Adoption Delta is wrong under its own set definitions. Using [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L539), with `B_A = {f1,f2,f3}`, `B_B = {f2,f4,f5}`, and `C_A = {f2,f4,f6}`, we get `A_drop = (B_A \\ B_B) \\ C_A = {f1,f3}`, so `Δ_drop = 2/2 = 1.0`, not `0.5` as stated at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L560). The reported `Δ̄ = 0.5` therefore does not follow from the example.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either correct the arithmetic to `Δ_drop = 1.0` and `Δ̄ = 0.75`, or change the example set `C_A` so that one of `{f1,f3}` is retained and the stated `0.5` result becomes true.
VERIFIED: TRUE
